title: Study on miR-155 Expression in Type 2 Diabetes and Vascular Complications
author: Liting Guo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tmkek4w

steps.title: Extract peripheral blood total RNA
steps.instruction: Extract total RNA from peripheral blood using the TRIzol method following the manufacturer's instructions.

substeps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration using an ultraviolet spectrophotometer.
Preserve samples with a 260/280 ratio between 1.8 and 2.1 at -80ºC.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Prepare the reverse transcriptase system using the stem ring method for miR-155 and U6 internal reference primers.

substeps.instruction: Combine the following reagents in DEPC water to a total volume of 12.5 µl: 1 µl dNTP (10 mM), 0.5 µl target gene reverse transcriptase primer, 0.5 µl internal parameter reverse transcriptase primer, 0.5 µl RNase inhibitor, 1 µl M-MLV, 4 µl 5× buffer, and 2 µg total RNA.
Incubate the mixture at 42ºC for 60 min and then at 70ºC for 15 min.
Maintain the resulting cDNA product at -20ºC.

steps.title: Perform fluorescence quantitative RT-PCR
steps.instruction: Set up the RT-PCR system using cDNA diluted 10 times.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the reaction mixture: 9 µl 2.5× SYBR Green Master Mix, 1 µl upstream primer, 1 µl downstream primer, 3 µl cDNA, and 6 µl DEPC water.

For miR-155, U6, and sICAM-1, apply the following thermal cycling conditions: predenaturation at 95°C for 20 s; 40 cycles of denaturation at 95°C for 10 s, annealing at 60°C for 20 s, and extension at 72°C for 15 s; final extension at 72°C for 5 min.
For NF-κB and GAPDH, use an annealing temperature of 57°C for 20 s, keeping all other thermal conditions identical to those used for miR-155, U6, and sICAM-1.
